title: ooRexx pitfalls met while building it
summary: Faults found and fixed in this lane, each a rule for the next change.
invariants: An attribute never set answers its own name in upper case (ID), not .nil: objects made by a session set unset attributes to .nil.
A literal followed by a blank and a symbol b or x can read as a binary or hex string ("...~"b "= ..."): use || b.
SIGNAL inside a DO loop ends every active loop: a label used by SIGNAL ON goes in a helper method, not inside a loop.
call self~x is not a message call: write self~x as a message instruction.
parse var s before "%" n +1 s: +1 counts from the start of the matched literal; split by hand.
A comment that contains a slash and star opens a nested comment (data/*.cls inside a comment).
A JSON boolean from ADDRESS FETCH JSON is a JSONBoolean: read its ~value.
SysFileTree answers absolute names: compare with an absolute destination (.File~new(d)~absolutePath).
A relative database path fails in the browser: oodBeside resolves it beside the program.
Values for SQL go through NoSQLServer's DatabasePreparedStatement and DatabaseParameterBinder typed from the catalogue: an untyped 1 became '1'.
Never name a DO OVER control variable label: DO LABEL names a loop, so do label over x parses as a loop named OVER and fails with Error 26.2 at run time.
A long property label makes the properties panel taller and scrolls the page; browser tests that drag between panels then miss. Keep labels short and put a format in the input's placeholder.

CALL sets SIGL to the CALL's line and drops RESULT when the routine returns nothing; a message instruction leaves SIGL alone. Code injected into user code (probes, hooks) must be a message, and must answer RESULT as it was.
.Package~new(name, source) in a test numbers its lines from the package start: compare two runs only when both are built the same way.

Rexx Parser 20261115 uses CATCH itself (BaseClassesAndRoutines, BIFs). On an ooRexx before r13514 it still loads and parses (those clauses read as commands that are not reached), but its error hints are lost. Ship its LICENSE-CPL: ANSI.ErrorText.cls is CPL 1.0.
Rexx Parser doc-comments (20261115 too): on a closing ' */' line after a tag, the '/' is classified as tag text; OxDocs drops it. Reported for Josep Maria Blasco.

RAISE without RETURN is an EXIT: it ends the whole program and raises the condition in the program's caller, so no SIGNAL ON, CALL ON or CATCH in the program sees it. RAISE ... RETURN raises it in the routine's caller; THROW (RFE #31) stays in its routine. Only RAISE SYNTAX is raised where it stands. (v0.18 published the opposite as an ooRexx observation; it was a test fault.)
